Three skills from dialectical behaviour therapy, the treatment with the strongest evidence for getting through emotional crises. They are for riding out the next few minutes — nothing more is being asked of you.
Stop. Take a step back. Observe what is happening, inside and around you. Proceed mindfully — pick the next small action, not the whole day.

Cold water on your face or hands. Intense movement for a minute. Paced breathing, out longer than in. Then relax each muscle group in turn. These change body chemistry fast when thinking alone will not.

The cold water and the hard movement both swing your heart rate on purpose. If you have a heart condition, an eating disorder, or are pregnant, skip those two and ask a doctor first. The paced breathing and the muscle relaxation are gentle, and they work on their own.

A grey screen is the single most effective change measured in this field — not through willpower, but because colour is most of what makes a feed feel alive. Trials consistently find people put the phone down sooner without it.
Android will not let an app turn this on by itself, which is the right rule. Run this once from a computer with the phone plugged in, and it sticks through reboots:

This borrows Android\'s colour correction, so the two cannot both be on at once. Whatever correction you had set is put back when the grey screen goes off. If you rely on it during the day, you may still want to leave the night setting alone.

MindAnchor is an open-source, research-backed launcher. It has no accounts, no server and no analytics — by default, your data never leaves this phone. The one opt-in exception is the COROS Training Hub bridge under Settings → Measuring: when you connect it, the launcher fetches HRV and resting heart rate from COROS, over an encrypted connection, with your COROS password held in this phone\'s secure Keystore. The connection is off until you turn it on. It is a wellness tool, not a medical device, and it is no substitute for talking to someone.

Some watches — COROS today — do not release every signal to Health Connect. This optional bridge fills the gaps. The launcher makes outbound calls to the COROS Training Hub (a third-party server) and stores your COROS email + password in this phone\'s secure Keystore for as long as the bridge stays connected. Disconnect wipes both. Off by default.

What goes to the COROS server: your email + password (for sign-in), the resulting access token, and the three data fetches (HRV, daily summary, activity list). What does not go anywhere else: nothing — this bridge is the only outbound channel and the launcher\'s promise of \"no other network call\" still holds.

Sign in once with your COROS Training Hub email + password. COROS requires the password as an MD5 hash, so that is what is sent, over an encrypted connection. The hash stands in for the password, so treat it with the same care.
Fetch the last 7 days of nightly HRV (RMSSD ms) and the last ~28 days of resting heart rate from the Training Hub every 6 hours.
Show the data on the wellness card, alongside the Health Connect data. Health Connect wins when both have a reading; COROS fills the gaps for the signals the watch does not release.
No analytics, no crash reports, no telemetry. The encrypted credential blob is the only thing on disk.
Does not sign out of the COROS phone app. The side-channel uses the Training Hub web API, not the mobile API, so your phone app stays signed in.

MindAnchor reads eight record types from Health Connect: heart rate, resting heart rate, HRV, sleep, steps, exercise, calories, mindfulness. None of it leaves this phone.

A 90-second fingertip reading gives the launcher a personal baseline. Without one, your numbers show up as a count of days — useful, but less personal.
